RULES

GOAL

Score the most points by connecting tiles of your color.

TURNS

A turn consists of a player picking up and placing a tile. The player may rotate the tile to any orientation before placing it.

A player may pick up the tile from the deck, the pool or their hand and may place it in the pool, in their hand or on the board.

A player may place multiple tiles during their turn if going from the deck to the pool, or from their hand to the board.

If a player has emptied their hand of tiles, they may place a tile from the pool as a bonus, which acts as an extension of their hand.

A player's turn is over when: they place a tile from the deck or pool onto the board, they place all tiles from their hand, they place a tile from their hand to the pool, or they pass. A player who passes once they have filled the pool with deck tiles as well as flipped the next deck tile, causes all six of those tiles to be discarded.

PLACEMENT

A player may freely place any tile they pick up on any open, unbordered space. If it is placed touching any other tile or tiles, adjacent edges must match color.

Gray and black are "wild card" edge colors. Gray may be placed against any color, and any color may be placed against it; black may be placed against any color, but once placed, only black may be placed against black.

SCORING

When two tiles are placed touching each other along matching edges, points are awarded to that color's player. Each one sixth tile wedge part of an area newly linked in this manner awards 1 point.

AURA

The placement on the board of a player's jewel creates an area out of the surrounding (up to) six open board spaces, known as its aura.

A player may extend their aura by placing a tile into their aura; any open space touching edges of that player's color on this tile become part of their aura.

Only the aura color's player may place tiles in their aura, and when they do so, are not bound by the normal tile placement requirements.

The exception to this is, a player may place a hand tile in an opponent's aura, but in that case it must meet normal tile placement requirements.

END

Once every space on the board is filled with a tile, the game enters overtime. The deck will now flip (up to) five tiles at once - automatically placed into the pool - from which the player may pick up one; the rest are discarded.

In overtime, players may "overwrite" tiles on the board, as long the tile placement complies with the normal adjacency requirements.

The game ends when there are no more tiles left to be played, or all three players pass on consecutive turns.

Full Rules

This is the exact reference sheet for the current game engine. The quick rules teach the game; this page settles edge cases.

Screen Breakdown

Setup

There are three players: red, blue, and green.

The center space is a neutral jewel display and is not playable.

The pool has 5 slots. Each player's hand has 3 slots.

Each player starts with one seeded starter jewel in their hand. When that jewel is placed on the board, it creates that player's initial aura.

Deck

The game uses a shuffled 100-tile deck built from red, green, blue, gray, and black sections.

Solids: 5 tile types, 4 copies each, for 20 tiles. A solid tile has all 6 edges the same color.

Bicolors: 10 tile types, 3 copies each, for 30 tiles. A bicolor tile has one 3-edge section of each of two colors.

Imbalanced tricolors: 20 tile types, 2 copies each, for 40 tiles. An imbalanced tricolor has one color on 4 edges and another color on 2 edges.

Balanced tricolors: 10 tile types, 1 copy each, for 10 tiles. A balanced tricolor has three colors, each covering 2 edges.

Altogether, the deck has 45 unique tile types. Starter jewels are seeded into player hands and are not drawn from the deck.

Deck Index

Unique tile faces are shown once with their deck multiplier. Starter jewels are seeded into player hands and are not part of the 100-tile deck.

Goal

Finish the game with the most points. The highest score wins. Ties are allowed.

Turns

On a turn, a player picks up one tile from the deck, their hand, or the pool. They may rotate the tile before placing it.

A tile may be placed onto the board, into the player's hand, or into the pool, as long as that destination is legal.

A selected deck tile must be resolved before the player selects another tile.

Only a hand tile placed onto the board starts hand-chain play. Moving a hand tile into the pool does not start the hand chain.

A hand-to-pool placement ends the turn unless it empties the player's hand during a hand-chain and unlocks the empty-hand pool bonus.

Occupied board spaces cannot be replaced during normal play. Once overtime or the deck-empty end phase begins, a legal placement may use an open space or replace an occupied non-jewel tile.

Deck And Pool

Before making a placement, a player may flip a deck tile and place it into any open pool slot.

After placing a deck tile into the pool, they may flip another deck tile. This can continue until the 5 pool slots are full.

Once the pool is full, the next flipped deck tile must be placed onto the board, placed into hand, or used with PASS to clear the pool.

Once a deck or pool tile is placed onto the board or into hand, the turn ends.

After a turn-ending human placement, the move remains undoable for 6 seconds. The Undo triangle counts down with a quiet clock tick when sound is on, then the move auto-confirms and the next turn begins.

When the final deck tile is flipped, it remains face-up in the deck slot and must be resolved before another tile source is chosen. It may be placed into pool, into hand, or onto the now-overwrite-able board. If the pool is full, the player may instead PASS to discard the full pool plus the final tile.

If a deck tile cannot legally be kept in hand or pool, it must be placed on the board if a legal board placement exists.

Hand Play

If a player begins their turn by placing a hand tile onto the board, they may continue placing hand tiles until their hand is empty, or until they stop the hand chain.

Because a hand has 3 slots, a full hand-chain can resolve up to all 3 hand tiles before any earned pool bonus.

During a hand-chain, hand tiles may continue going onto the board. A hand tile may also be moved into an open pool slot, but that stops the hand chain.

If the hand-to-pool move empties the hand during the chain, the empty-hand pool bonus is still earned.

A player may use PASS to stop hand play early. Remaining hand tiles stay in hand.

When a player empties their hand during hand-chain play, they earn one bonus pool tile if a legal pool tile is available.

The bonus pool tile acts like a hand tile for board-placement rules, but it must be placed directly onto the board. It cannot be stored in hand.

Passing

If the pool is full and the player has selected a flipped deck tile, PASS discards the full pool plus that deck tile and ends the turn.

PASS can also end hand play early, decline an earned bonus pool tile, or discard overtime pool choices. Hand-play opt-outs do not count toward the three-pass game end.

Three consecutive no-placement or pool-clearing PASS turns end the game.

Placement

A tile may be placed on any open board space, except the center space, if every edge touching another tile is legal.

Matching colors may touch edge-to-edge.

Gray is wild against normal colors and may touch a newly placed black edge, but gray does not bypass an already-placed black edge.

Black is wild when placed. After black is on the board, only black may touch that black edge.

Scoring

Players score when tile sections of their color are linked to matching sections across tile edges.

Think of each 1/6th tile section as 1 point. A linked tile can contribute 2, 3, 4, or 6 points depending on how much of that tile's color is linked.

One tricolor section is worth 2. One bicolor section is worth 3. Two same-color tricolor sections are worth 4. A solid or jewel tile is worth 6.

Gray and black do not score and do not create scoring links.

Isolated color sections do not score until they link to another tile by a matching edge.

Scores are recalculated from the whole board after each placement.

Initial Aura

Each player's initial jewel captures the 6 spaces around it when placed on the board. These spaces are that player's initial aura.

A starter jewel may not be placed where its initial aura would overlap another initial jewel aura or the protected center ring.

A player may place freely inside their own aura. Normal edge-matching rules do not block that placement.

Only one seeded starter jewel per player may be placed and scored.

Opponent Aura

A player may not normally place a tile in another player's aura.

Exception: a player may place a hand tile into another player's aura if the tile follows normal board-placement rules.

Deck and pool tiles cannot enter another player's aura directly.

Expanded Aura

When a tile is placed in a player's own aura, that tile can expand the player's aura.

Any open space touching that player's color on the aura-placed tile becomes part of the expanded aura.

Only the player's own color edges project aura. Gray, black, and opponent-colored edges do not project aura for that player.

Expanded auras may overlap, including over initial aura spaces.

When auras compete, the color with the most aura claims touching the space controls it. Ties make the space neutral again.

A starter jewel creates the first aura claims by itself; after that, those claims compete like any other aura claim.

End Of Game

When every open board space is filled and tiles remain, overtime begins.

At the start of an overtime turn, deck tiles are revealed into the open pool slots. If the pool is already full, its existing tiles become the choices for that turn.

The player may choose one pool tile and place it on the board or into their hand. Choosing a tile ends the turn and discards the other pool choices. The player may also PASS to discard all the choices.

During overtime, a tile may replace any occupied non-jewel tile. The new tile must follow the normal edge-matching rules. The replaced tile is discarded.

A less common cleanup begins if the deck runs out before the board is full. The final deck tile must be resolved into the pool, into the player's hand, onto a legal board space, or by the normal full-pool PASS that discards the pool plus the revealed tile. No new pool tiles are revealed after this. Players continue using only the tiles already in their hands and the pool, and may replace occupied non-jewel tiles even while open spaces remain.

The game ends when no tiles remain to be played, or when all three players pass on consecutive turns without placing a tile on the board.
